riley_cs: Quick—customer kickoff in 12h. They want a tiny ops cheatbox (single sheet) that we can hand to their infra/ops folks. Needs: prefill how-to, safe batching defaults, KV cache guidance, streaming tips, 72h watchlist, and three fast mitigation steps. Keep it non-technical.

sam_se: I'll draft the cheatbox. One page, copy/paste snippets only, no internal flags.

ina_sre: Include a short degraded run order: route, throttles, fallback. Also a short explanation of how to read the KV hit metric.

jo_support: I'll add the top 5 questions we've seen and 1-line answers.

harry_pm: Add a single-sentence renewal-risk threshold and an escalation hook.

sam_se: Drafting now. Paste below (ops-friendly):

sam_se: "Kickoff Cheatbox  Ops TL;DR (one sheet)
- Goal: get safe baseline in first 72h; catch cost or latency regressions early.
- Quick prefill (copy/paste):
  for i in $(seq 1 120); do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \n    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n    -d '{\"prompt\":\"hello\",\"max_tokens\":64,\"metadata\":{\"prefill\":true}}' &
  done; wait
- Safe batching defaults (hosted + dedicated):
  * short prompts (<80 tokens): target_batch_size=20, max_batch_wait_ms=25
  * long outputs (>512 tokens): target_batch_size=4, max_batch_wait_ms=10 (avoid extra delay)
- KV cache guidance: enable prefix_cache=true; default prefix_ttl_seconds=300 for interactive, 45s for high-churn flows
  * How to read hit rate: prefix_cache_hit_rate is % of requests that used cached tokens. Aim for >40% after a 10-20m prefill.
- Streaming: enable when average output >512 tokens; set keepalive_seconds=12 and socket_timeout_ms=45000 to reduce mobile stalls
- Cost controls: configure daily_token_limit + per_minute_cap. Add webhook to alerting endpoint at 60% usage.
  * Example alert rule (Console): "tokens_consumed_today > daily_token_limit * 0.6 -> webhook /ops/cost-alerts"
- 72h watchlist (first 72h signals):
  1) tokens/day > baseline * 1.35 for 24h
  2) P95 latency > SLO for 2+ hours
  3) sustained 5xx rate > 1% for 30+ minutes
- Fast mitigations (execute in order, should be doable by ops):
  1) Switch routing to alternate region with spare capacity (Console routing -> failover).
  2) Enable throttles: set per-client_rate_limit to 100 req/min and reduce daily_token_limit if needed.
  3) Roll to compact fallback model (labelled "compact fallback" in Console) and reduce max_generation_tokens by 25%.
- What to capture for support: sample request JSON, route.name, account_id, X-Request-ID, prompt_hash, and timestamp.
- Escalation: If two watchlist signals appear in 72h, open a ticket with tag cs:kickoff-review. CS will coordinate an emergency config audit and short-term protections.
"

jo_support: Top-5 FAQs (one line each):
1) Tokens suddenly spiked after launch? -> Usually repeated full prompts or verbose system text; enable client dedupe + prefill.
2) Warm pool not helping? -> Confirm prefix_cache_hit_rate and compare warm vs cold median latency.
3) Streaming stalls on mobile? -> Increase keepalive_seconds and verify LB/proxy passthrough for long-lived connections.
4) How to stop runaway spend during test? -> Use daily_token_limit + per_minute_cap + webhook alert at 60%.
5) Latency variance high? -> Check batch sizes and prefix_cache_hit_rate; consider reducing max_batch_tokens.

nina_sre: Mini validation commands to run (ops can copy-paste):
- Check KV hit rate: curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/metrics?name=prefix_cache_hit_rate
- Compare warm vs cold: run `aburst 30 warm_requests.json` then `aburst 30 cold_requests.json` and compare median latencies
- Verify alerts: simulate token burn to 61% and confirm webhook fires to /ops/costs

harry_pm: Renewal-risk callout (customer-facing): if two of the 72h watchlist signals trigger, we treat as elevated renewal risk and convene CS+Eng within 24h. We'll offer a config review and temporary protections.
